findings.title: The record is allocated to its bearer
findings.claim: The dative phrase directs the brought-out record to the same individual whose person-bound trace was named in the first clause.
findings.mechanism: Lahu depends on nukhriju, and its third-person suffix points back to insan; appearing before the Day-frame makes the individual recipient visible before the time of disclosure is named.
findings.reader_payoff: The document is encountered as individually addressed rather than displayed to an unspecified audience.
findings.containment: The phrase permits recipient, target, or allocated-party force; it does not decide whether the record benefits or indicts its bearer.

epistemic.reason: The local preposition, suffix, and clause relation directly support personal allocation.

findings.title: Allocation leaves the outcome open
findings.claim: Lahu assigns the record to the individual while leaving open whether it is for or against him.
findings.mechanism: The preposition marks the individual as recipient or target; the record and resurrection-day trigger a judgment setting in which either valence can matter, but the suffix itself does not supply the verdict.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees personal address without being told the judgment's result.
findings.containment: Neither favorable nor adverse outcome is selected, and the preposition alone does not mean condemnation.

epistemic.reason: The allocation is grammatical; its for/against coloring depends on the judgment scene.

findings.title: One person remains the referent
findings.claim: The repeated third-person forms keep one human as the bearer through binding, possession, body-site, allocation, and encounter.
findings.mechanism: The object suffix on alzamnahu and possessives on tairahu and unuquhi track insan; lahu returns the extracted record to him, and yalqahu presents that same person meeting it.
findings.reader_payoff: The successive stages remain attached to one accountable individual instead of dispersing across different actors.
findings.containment: The chain establishes a shared referent within this ayah; it does not itself make claims about other passages.

epistemic.reason: The suffix sequence and singular antecedent are explicit in the aligned focus morphology.

findings.title: The day is an event-time

findings.mechanism: The accusative yawma frames nukhriju, while its definite genitive complement names the resurrection event; the construct relation changes an open day-range into the time of disclosure.
findings.reader_payoff: The record's production is placed at a named eschatological event, not at an unspecified daytime.
findings.containment: Yawma remains a day or time noun; the event reading is selected by its local complement, not by a free root association.

epistemic.reason: Case, construct syntax, and the following event noun supply the selection locally.

findings.title: Totality is distributed over persons
findings.claim: Kulla takes singular insan as its domain, making the accountability rule comprehensive across persons one by one.
findings.mechanism: The totality quantifier precedes and governs the singular human noun; this relation changes an unbounded 'all' into exhaustive scope over each individual bearer.
findings.reader_payoff: No human is left outside the scene, yet the scope is experienced person by person rather than as an undifferentiated mass.
findings.containment: Only the local quantifier and human domain are retained; no cosmic transition or later ethical rule is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The quantifier and its singular human complement directly establish distributive scope.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyin parçalarının veya bir kümedeki bireylerin hiçbirini dışarıda bırakmadan kapsanması çekirdektir.
branch_activations.carrier: Kulla carries exhaustive totality.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The following singular insan supplies the human domain.
branch_activations.activation: The quantifier's whole scope meets an individual human noun.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Every person is included as an individual bearer.
branch_activations.boundary: This is distributive scope over humans, not collective mass.

findings.title: Scope arrives before the act
findings.claim: The fronted accusative quantifier establishes the full human scope before the binding verb states what happens to each person.
findings.mechanism: Kulla appears before alzamnahu and governs singular insan; the syntax first lays out the complete set, then applies the binding act across its individual members.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader encounters the universal reach before the action, with each human still countable as a separate case.
findings.containment: The claim concerns local order and distribution; it does not claim a preceding cosmic scale is active.

epistemic.reason: Accusative case, fronting, and the singular complement are explicit in the focus morphology.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyin parçalarının veya bir kümedeki bireylerin hiçbirini dışarıda bırakmadan kapsanması çekirdektir.
branch_activations.carrier: Kulla carries the complete scope placed at the front.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Insan supplies the individual domain and alzamnahu supplies the act applied to it.
branch_activations.activation: Fronted totality is distributed over each human before the binding clause unfolds.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The universal scope is established ahead of the act.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch remains exhaustive scope, not a process of completion.

findings.title: A variant recasts the opening
findings.claim: The nominative variant would make the opening more topic-like, while the local accusative keeps kulla as a fronted object resumed by the verb.
findings.mechanism: The case shift changes how the quantifier relates to the following clause: nominative permits a topic-comment frame, whereas the accusative depends on the verbal construction and places scope before the act.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how a small case difference changes the ayah's opening architecture.
findings.containment: This preserves both the variant's contrast and the supplied local case without choosing a variant reading.

epistemic.reason: The local case is grounded in the focus morphology; the alternate architecture is variant evidence.

findings.title: The person meets a perceivable record
findings.claim: The open personal record lets insan appear as a perceiving self confronting an external representation of its own account.
findings.mechanism: Insan names the person who is individually bound; kitab is brought out for that person, yalqahu makes the record directly met, and manshuran presents it already open. Together these independent focus forms make recognition available as an analogical relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The record can be felt as a mirror of the person's own account rather than as an anonymous document.
findings.containment: No seeing or reading verb appears here, and the disputed forgetfulness association is not asserted; the eye/perception branch is analogical and insan still means a human person.

epistemic.reason: The open-record contact is focus-local, but perceiving a self-image is an analogical reading and forgetting is not stated.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: görerek fark etme; bağlama göre işitme, sezme ve bakıp araştırma
branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyi gözle görerek fark etmeyi veya seçmeyi anlatır.
branch_activations.carrier: Insan names the individual who bears the record.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The written book is brought out for him, directly met, and already open.
branch_activations.activation: A person and a visible, personally addressed record make recognition possible by analogy.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The person can meet the record as a perceiving self confronting an account of itself.
branch_activations.boundary: No act of looking or reading is grammatically stated; this is not the lexical definition of insan.

findings.title: The human anchors later suffixes
findings.claim: The singular human noun supplies one antecedent for the later object, possessive, dative, and encounter references.
findings.mechanism: The indefinite singular insan is followed by a chain of third-person forms on binding, omen, neck, allocation, and encounter; the noun anchors their repeated return to the same individual.
findings.reader_payoff: The whole accountability sequence stays enclosed around one person.
findings.containment: Only the focus ayah's local antecedence is retained; no same-surah document arc is inferred.

epistemic.reason: The singular noun and subsequent suffixes align within the focus ayah.

findings.title: Each human is a complete instance
findings.claim: The singular indefinite insan gives kulla a countable human domain, so universal liability lands on each person as a complete instance.
findings.mechanism: Kulla governs the singular genitive insan; the singular pronouns that follow keep the individual bearer present through the remaining clauses.
findings.reader_payoff: The rule's universality and its individualized application arrive together.
findings.containment: The singular form supports an individual case within exhaustive scope, without limiting the statement to one named person.

epistemic.reason: The singular noun, quantifier relation, and following pronouns are explicit.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: insan türü ve bu türden bir kişi
branch_activations.facet_statement: İnsan türünü, insanların oluşturduğu topluluğu veya bu türün tek bir üyesini görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşısında adlandırır.
branch_activations.carrier: Insan names the human kind or an individual member of it.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Kulla quantifies the human domain and the later suffix tracks its individual member.
branch_activations.activation: The human noun's individual reading meets distributive totality and singular reference.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Each person is treated as an individual bearer, not as an undifferentiated collective.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch identifies a human person; it does not add awareness or sociability.

findings.title: Binding is already complete
findings.claim: The Form IV perfect verb presents the binding as completed before the later record is brought out.
findings.mechanism: Alzamnahu combines a first-person plural subject with a singular human object and an imposed second object; its perfect aspect makes attachment precede the future disclosure clause.
findings.reader_payoff: The first clause establishes a finished attachment before the second clause opens the disclosure scene.
findings.containment: The completed act is local to this verb; no comparative claim about another divine binding scene is retained.

epistemic.reason: Form, aspect, agent, and object roles are supplied in the focus morphology.

findings.title: The binding is imposed
findings.claim: The Form IV binding makes the person's relation to the named tair imposed and obligatory rather than merely observed.
findings.mechanism: The l-z-m root contributes attachment and necessity, while the causative Form IV acts on the human object and binds the possessed tair; the neck phrase gives that obligation a bodily location.
findings.reader_payoff: The person is shown carrying an imposed relation, not simply noticing a sign.
findings.containment: The verb supports binding and obligation here; no separate legal ruling or outcome is selected.

epistemic.reason: The local causative form, root range, object suffix, and neck relation converge.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi, kendisine dışarıdan yöneltilen bir işlemle belirli bir şeyden sorumlu veya ona uymakla yükümlü hale getirilir.
branch_activations.carrier: Alzamnahu is a causative act that makes the person bound to something.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The possessed tair and its neck location identify what the operation binds.
branch_activations.activation: The Form IV verb's imposed force meets the personal object and bodily locus.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The person's relation to the consequence is imposed, not merely noticed.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a binding operation, not the separate branch of a continuing attached state.

findings.title: The binding verb sounds compact
findings.claim: The compact l-z-m-n consonant run gives the binding verb a hardened, compressed sound contour.
findings.mechanism: The consonants are packed into alzamnahu at the point where the ayah imposes attachment; the sound note lets the ear feel closure alongside the verb's binding meaning.
findings.reader_payoff: The act of fastening has an audible pressure in the word itself.
findings.containment: This is a phonetic impression, not proof that consonants encode the meaning or that the sound dictates interpretation.

epistemic.reason: The consonant sequence is present; its matching pressure is a perceptual reading.

findings.title: Flight remains inside the personal lot
findings.claim: Tairahu keeps a flying or bird image audible inside the person's assigned lot or consequence.
findings.mechanism: The active-participle form carries flight into the possessed noun; alzamnahu treats it as an imposed object and fi unuqi places it at the person's own neck, so motion and personal fate meet in one image.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can retain the flying image while seeing the consequence fixed to its bearer.
findings.containment: The bird or flight image does not make an actual bird appear; the local object remains an individual's lot or consequence.

epistemic.reason: The form and local binding scene support the layered image, while the literal referent remains a personal consequence.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kanatlı canlı ve onun havada ilerleme hareketi dalın ortak çekirdeğidir.
branch_activations.carrier: Tairahu carries the active-participle flight or flying-thing image.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The binding verb and neck phrase place that mobile image on the individual.
branch_activations.activation: Flight meets imposed attachment and bodily location.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The person's lot remains imaginable as something mobile that is made to accompany him.
branch_activations.boundary: The word's local consequence sense remains intact; no physical bird is required.

findings.title: A variant foregrounds the bird
findings.claim: The supplied concrete-bird variant foregrounds a bird noun, while the local active-participle form keeps the flying image in motion.
findings.mechanism: The variant changes the form's foreground from an active participant to a concrete bird; the neck-bound scene can hold that contrast alongside the personal-fate sense without forcing the referent to be literal.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear both a concrete bird image and a motion-bearing omen image in the supplied form evidence.
findings.containment: The variant is contrastive evidence and does not replace the aligned surface or require a literal bird in the scene.

epistemic.reason: The variant contrast is explicit, but it remains an alternate form rather than the aligned local reading.

findings.title: A catch interrupts the flight word
findings.claim: The hamza gives tairahu an audible catch just before the ayah describes it as bound.
findings.mechanism: The glottal stop interrupts the flight-bearing word's sound; alzamnahu and the neck phrase then arrest that mobile image in the syntax of attachment.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears a small interruption where the scene itself shifts from movement to binding.
findings.containment: The sound is a listening impression, not an extra morpheme or proof of a semantic meaning.

epistemic.reason: The sound shape and following bind are local; the interpretive match between them is exploratory.

findings.title: The personal sign becomes a record
findings.claim: The ayah turns the hidden, moving personal tair into a written record that can be met already open.
findings.mechanism: Tairahu is the imposed second object at the neck; nukhriju introduces kitab as a new object for the same person, and manshuran supplies its exposed final state. The successive relations change the image from personal consequence to inspectable evidence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees one accountability object pass from attachment into disclosure rather than having a book appear without a link.
findings.containment: The sequence is local to these clauses; it does not assert a physical bird changing into a book.

epistemic.reason: The shared personal suffixes, coordinated clauses, record object, and final open-state participle support the transformation.

findings.title: The consequence belongs to its bearer
findings.claim: The possessed tair is the individual's own imposed object, not a transferable general destiny.
findings.mechanism: Alzamnahu governs the possessed noun tairahu as its second object; the attached third-person suffix links it to insan, and the neck phrase locates that same object on its bearer.
findings.reader_payoff: The consequence is personally localized before the book is brought out.
findings.containment: The claim is about grammatical possession and placement; it does not define a general doctrine of destiny.

epistemic.reason: The second-object relation, possessive suffix, and neck phrase are explicit.

findings.title: The neck phrase allows two placements
findings.claim: Fi unuqi can be heard as locating the fastening on the neck or as locating the possessed tair there, with the binding verb remaining the syntactic head.
findings.mechanism: The preposition governs the neck noun and relates it to alzamnahu; either the attachment action is located there or the omen itself stands there, so both construals make the personal body-site concrete.
findings.reader_payoff: The burden is visible as placed at the bearer rather than floating as an abstract possession.
findings.containment: The two locative construals coexist within the focus wording; neither turns the neck into a separate actor.

epistemic.reason: The prepositional relation is direct, while the two scene construals remain interpretive.

findings.title: The neck gives attachment a body-site
findings.claim: The possessed neck gives the abstract personal consequence a concrete body-site.
findings.mechanism: The neck noun is governed by fi and bears the same third-person possessor as the human object; alzamnahu independently supplies the binding action, so the body-site localizes what is imposed.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees responsibility as borne at the person's own body, not merely held in the abstract.
findings.containment: The focus word names the anatomical neck; any burden effect is a scene reading, not a new literal object.

epistemic.reason: The preposition, body-part noun, and possessive suffix directly support the location.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: baş ile gövde arasındaki boyun ve boyuna bağlı nitelikler
branch_activations.facet_statement: Baş ile gövde arasında bağlantı kuran beden uzvudur.
branch_activations.carrier: Unuqi names the bodily neck connecting head and torso.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Alzamnahu binds the person's tair and fi places that relation at this body-site.
branch_activations.activation: The actual body part meets an imposed object and a locative preposition.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The consequence has a visible personal locus.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch is the anatomical neck, not a neck-shaped landscape or social group.

findings.title: Attachment becomes a worn burden
findings.claim: The neck-bound attachment can be imagined as a collar-like burden worn at a vulnerable body-site.
findings.mechanism: Alzamnahu supplies binding, tairahu supplies the personal object, and the possessed neck gives it a place to be carried; their contact changes an abstract liability into a felt bodily load.
findings.reader_payoff: Accountability becomes visible as something the person bears on their own body.
findings.containment: No literal collar or shackle appears, and the objects in other neck scenes are not imported into this image.

epistemic.reason: The body-site and binding are explicit; the collar-like load is a bounded analogy.

findings.title: The body-site belongs to this person
findings.claim: The possessive suffix makes the neck the individual's own body-site for the attached consequence.
findings.mechanism: The singular neck noun bears the third-person suffix and depends on fi; the human antecedent and repeated pronouns keep this locus attached to one bearer.
findings.reader_payoff: The accountability image is individualized down to the body part on which it is located.
findings.containment: Ownership is grammatical and personal; it does not imply transfer of a burden to another person's body.

epistemic.reason: Number, possession, and local pronoun reference are directly supported.

findings.title: The conjunction opens disclosure
findings.claim: The second conjunction keeps the binding and disclosure clauses linked while opening a new future scene.
findings.mechanism: Waw joins alzamnahu's completed act to nukhriju's imperfect Form IV; the coordination preserves continuity but shifts the temporal scene from established attachment to future production.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader experiences the two stages as one connected sequence.
findings.containment: The hinge relation is within 17:13 and does not depend on the next verse.

epistemic.reason: The conjunction and contrasting verb forms are visible in the focus morphology.

findings.title: Variants shift extraction's agent
findings.claim: The local Form IV presents the record as actively brought out by the plural speaker, while variants can shift the disclosure toward passive, singular-agent, or self-emergent action.
findings.mechanism: Nukhriju is imperfect, Form IV, and first-person plural with kitab as its object; alternate morphology changes who appears to cause the record's emergence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the agency carried by the local verb while keeping variant pressures visible.
findings.containment: The variant possibilities remain counter-readings; the focus form is not displaced and no agency option is ranked.

epistemic.reason: The supplied local morphology is clear; the contrasting agency forms are variant evidence.

findings.title: The record is actively brought out
findings.claim: Nukhriju presents the written record as something actively brought out for the individual.
findings.mechanism: The first-person plural Form IV verb governs kitab as its object; its imperfect aspect opens a future disclosure scene after the completed attachment.
findings.reader_payoff: The record emerges through an act rather than appearing as a neutral object.
findings.containment: The focus supports caused bringing-out by the plural speaker; the manner or hidden location is not specified.

epistemic.reason: Voice, form, aspect, and object relation are supplied by the aligned focus morphology.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: bir şeyi çıkarma, elde etme veya yetiştirme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir etken, başka bir varlığı bulunduğu yerden çıkarır veya görünür duruma getirir.
branch_activations.carrier: Nukhriju actively brings an object out or into view.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Kitab supplies the thing brought out.
branch_activations.activation: The transitive extraction verb directly acts on the written record.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The individual is given a record through caused disclosure.
branch_activations.boundary: No particular concealed location is asserted.

findings.title: Extraction meets the Day of Rising
findings.claim: The bringing-out verb gains an eschatological emergence coloring because the focus clause locates it on the Day of Rising.
findings.mechanism: Nukhriju carries caused extraction and al-qiyamah names the resurrection event; their independent focus-word contact makes disclosure sound like emergence into an account scene while the object remains kitab.
findings.reader_payoff: The record's appearance is felt as part of resurrectional disclosure, not a neutral production.
findings.containment: This is a focus-local cross-root resonance; no parallel verse or further movement system is required.

epistemic.reason: The local Day of Rising supplies the trigger, while the extraction-to-resurrection coloring remains a resonance.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: bir şeyi çıkarma, elde etme veya yetiştirme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir etken, başka bir varlığı bulunduğu yerden çıkarır veya görünür duruma getirir.
branch_activations.carrier: Nukhriju carries the event of bringing the personal record out.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Al-qiyamah names resurrection and kitab is the object disclosed.
branch_activations.activation: The extraction verb and Day of Rising meet within the same focus clause.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Disclosure can be heard as eschatological emergence.
branch_activations.boundary: The record remains the object; no external resurrection parallel is imported.

findings.title: A mobile trace is fixed and disclosed
findings.claim: From an attached omen or deed-record that is later shown as a book, the focus stages a mobile personal trace being fixed to the body, brought out, written, met, and opened.
findings.mechanism: Kulla distributes the scene to every insan; alzamnahu makes the personal tair remain with its bearer at the neck, while nukhriju changes its attached latency into a visible kitab. The written object is then met directly and described as already manshuran, so the mobile image ends as exposed evidence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader perceives a trajectory changing state from mobile sign to bodily attachment to a record the bearer must face.
findings.containment: This is an attributed reading of the focus sequence. Flight is carried by tairahu, but light dispersal is excluded; kitab remains a personal record, and no literal bird, light, or physical trajectory is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The trace coordinates agree with the focus QAC surface and its several contacts are locally grounded; legacy_unbound provenance keeps the synthesis attributed.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyin parçalarının veya bir kümedeki bireylerin hiçbirini dışarıda bırakmadan kapsanması çekirdektir.
branch_activations.carrier: Kulla supplies comprehensive scope over the focus statement.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The singular human noun insan gives that scope its individual domain.
branch_activations.activation: Universal totality contacts one-by-one human reference.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: No human falls outside the attached-and-disclosed sequence.
branch_activations.boundary: The quantifier is distributive here, not a collective mass.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Birliktelik veya bağlılık süreklidir; bağlı olan şey yerini ya da durumunu korur ve eşlik ettiği şeyden ayrılmaz.
branch_activations.carrier: Alzamnahu imposes attachment through the Form IV verb.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Tairahu is the personal object and the neck gives that attachment a body-site.
branch_activations.activation: The named mobile consequence meets a verb whose result keeps it with its bearer.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The trajectory becomes something that does not leave the person.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus uses a causative act; this branch describes its continuing result.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kanatlı canlı ve onun havada ilerleme hareketi dalın ortak çekirdeğidir.
branch_activations.carrier: Tairahu retains the flying-thing or flight image.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Binding, neck placement, and the final open record independently constrain that movement.
branch_activations.activation: The flight image meets successive acts that arrest and expose it.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: A mobile personal trace is fixed and later displayed.
branch_activations.boundary: The carrier supports flight, not the excluded light-dispersal branch.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: baş ile gövde arasındaki boyun ve boyuna bağlı nitelikler
branch_activations.facet_statement: Baş ile gövde arasında bağlantı kuran beden uzvudur.
branch_activations.carrier: Unuqi is the body's neck and personal locus.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Alzamnahu binds the person's tairahu to that locus.
branch_activations.activation: The mobile object and binding act meet at the actual body part.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The trace acquires a visible personal location.
branch_activations.boundary: No other neck-related branch is asserted.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: bir şeyi çıkarma, elde etme veya yetiştirme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir etken, başka bir varlığı bulunduğu yerden çıkarır veya görünür duruma getirir.
branch_activations.carrier: Nukhriju actively brings another object out or into view.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Kitab names the object produced by the extraction.
branch_activations.activation: The caused movement meets its written result.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The attached trace is externalized as a record.
branch_activations.boundary: The verb supports bringing-out, not a specified concealed location.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: bir şeyi çıkarma, elde etme veya yetiştirme
branch_activations.facet_statement: İşlem, saklı ya da örtük bir şeyi çıkarıp elde etme biçiminde gerçekleşebilir.
branch_activations.carrier: Nukhriju carries the act of extracting or obtaining.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The bound personal tair is later rendered as a kitab, giving the extraction an earlier latent object.
branch_activations.activation: The attached trace and the brought-out record connect latent attachment to inspectable evidence.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: What was bound to the person becomes available for inspection.
branch_activations.boundary: Concealment is an attributed implication of extraction, not a separately named place.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel işlem, harfleri yazıyla düzenleyip bir metin oluşturmak veya var olan metni kopyalamaktır.
branch_activations.carrier: Kitab carries an ordered written text.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Nukhriju brings it out and manshuran presents its exposed state.
branch_activations.activation: The writing operation and the open written product meet in the same record.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The trace takes stable written form.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus names the product; it does not narrate the writing act.

branch_activations.facet_statement: İşlemin ürünü, yazılmış metin veya üzerinde bu metnin bulunduğu sayfa ya da kitaptır.
branch_activations.carrier: Kitab is the written product brought out for the person.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The extraction verb and open-state participle make that product inspectable.
branch_activations.activation: A written object meets the act of disclosure and the state of spreading.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The attached trace is presented as a readable document.
branch_activations.boundary: The record is not identified as a revealed Book.

branch_activations.facet_statement: İki kişi veya şey karşı karşıya gelir ya da biri ötekiyle rastlaşır.
branch_activations.carrier: Yalqa presents the bearer as encountering the record.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Kitab is its object and manshuran gives the object an exposed state.
branch_activations.activation: The direct meeting meets a document already available to be faced.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Reception becomes unavoidable face-to-face encounter.
branch_activations.boundary: The verb does not itself declare whether the result favors or harms the person.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kumaş, kitap, sayfa, eşya veya bulut gibi bir şeyi açmak, sermek ve yüzeye yaymak temel işlemdir.
branch_activations.carrier: Manshuran describes the record as opened and spread.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The written kitab and earlier mobile tair provide the object sequence it closes.
branch_activations.activation: The open document completes the change from mobile trace to inspectable record.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The trajectory ends in full exposure before its bearer.
branch_activations.boundary: The word describes an open record; it does not say how many pages it contains.

findings.title: The book operates as borne liability
findings.claim: The book is not only a report of what belongs to a person: read with the already completed binding and bodily locus, it can carry the force of liability the bearer undergoes on the Day of Rising.
findings.mechanism: Form IV alzamnahu makes the person answerable to a bound object at his own neck; kitab can carry written establishment and judgment, al-qiyamah names the event of resurrection and judgment, and yalqahu makes the bearer meet and undergo the record's result. These focus words turn attachment into operative personal consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The document can be perceived as a liability already borne and then made manifest in the bearer's encounter.
findings.containment: This attributed reading adds legal force to the personal record without making every kitab a decree or deciding whether the individual receives good or harm.

epistemic.reason: Every coordinate and root in the trace aligns with the supplied focus surface, but the source identity is legacy_unbound and the judgment-force reading remains attributed.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: baş ile gövde arasındaki boyun ve boyuna bağlı nitelikler
branch_activations.facet_statement: Baş ile gövde arasında bağlantı kuran beden uzvudur.
branch_activations.carrier: The possessive neck is the individual's actual body-site.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The imposed binding verb and personal book attach liability to that bearer.
branch_activations.activation: The body's own neck meets the binding and the record that later represents its consequence.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Liability is bodily borne and individually identifiable.
branch_activations.boundary: No extra physical chain or shackle is asserted.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi, kendisine dışarıdan yöneltilen bir işlemle belirli bir şeyden sorumlu veya ona uymakla yükümlü hale getirilir.
branch_activations.carrier: Alzamnahu makes an object binding on a person through an externally directed act.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The neck and written record give the imposed relation personal location and content.
branch_activations.activation: Causative binding contacts the bodily locus and the document that later exposes it.

findings.title: The open book can act as a self-image
findings.claim: The person can meet the open book as a written self-image: an articulated counterpart that makes the person's own account difficult to disown.
findings.mechanism: Insan supplies the human carrier, kitab supplies stable written content, yalqahu makes the person meet that content directly, and manshuran presents it open for inspection. Their contact supports a self-reflexive analogy in which an external document functions as the person's counterpart.
findings.reader_payoff: The record can be perceived as returning the person's own life to them in a form they must face.
findings.containment: This remains the source's exploratory self-image resonance. The focus names no eye or literal mirror; insan retains its human-person sense, kitab remains a record, and no seal condition or number of pages is claimed.
